summary: The bill amends ERISA to bar the Labor Secretary from issuing rules that limit the range or types of investments fiduciaries may offer through self-directed brokerage windows in participant-directed retirement plans.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends ERISA fiduciary rules for retirement plan investments but contains no provisions related to federal expenditures, appropriations, or budget outlays. It neither authorizes nor restricts government spending.
No provisions address tax rates, credits, deductions, or revenue collection. The legislation is confined to investment selection rules under ERISA.
The bill does not mention health insurance, medical providers, coverage mandates, or any aspect of the healthcare system.
No reference to firearms, gun ownership, or related regulations appears in the text.
The legislation contains no immigration, border, or visa provisions.
No language pertains to reproductive health services or abortion access.
The bill does not address defense budgets, military procurement, or national security spending.

While the bill bars fiduciaries from favoring or disfavoring investments on non-risk-return grounds, it does not directly regulate environmental standards, emissions, or conservation policy. Any indirect effect on ESG investing is too attenuated to constitute genuine engagement with the topic.
Although the bill concerns retirement accounts, it does not alter eligibility, benefit levels, or funding for means-tested welfare programs such as SNAP or TANF.
No provisions relate to schools, student aid, or education policy.
The text contains no references to controlled substances, decriminalization, or enforcement.
No criminal penalties, sentencing rules, or policing measures are addressed.
The bill does not mention tariffs, trade agreements, or import/export rules.
No fiscal policy, deficit targets, or debt-ceiling provisions are present.
The legislation does not address civil rights, nondiscrimination rules, or protections based on sexual orientation or gender identity.
No foreign assistance, international development, or aid appropriations are mentioned.
The bill contains no election administration, voting access, or campaign finance provisions.
No data privacy, cybersecurity, or technology regulation language appears.

The bill modifies fiduciary standards under ERISA for participant-directed accounts but does not alter collective bargaining rights, union organizing rules, or union governance. The connection to labor unions is therefore nonexistent.
No provisions address religious exemptions, conscience protections, or conflicts between civil rights statutes and religious exercise.
